applicable_failures: The single awk call only re-filters the saved scan file (/tmp/work/wc_scan.txt) by `$2 ~ /^WC=[1-9]/`. That is a follow-up filter on the earlier output, and the stage never shows that the scan covered every matter. Matters 1001-1008 and 1045-1046 appear in search results with no WC hit and no opened file, so scan completeness is unverified.
The candidate set rests on the exact phrase count WC, which can miss matters whose attribution is worded differently or sits in metadata. No broader check was run.
critique.concerns: The re-derivation reads only the saved scan and cannot show that the scan itself reached all 266 matters. Whether the WC pattern was exact, or whether any matter timed out or errored, is not visible here. The 11 matters are scan hits only, and no document has been opened. HOLDS and ISSUEDLIKE counts of 0-3 are keyword counts, not proof that a hold was issued. 1035-00001 has HOLDS=0.
critique.recommendation: Do not rescan the whole store. First check the scan file's line count and error or timeout rows against the 266 matters. Then open the proof documents (hold notices, attribution records) for all 11 matters, including 1035-00001 and the low-count ones, and confirm practice attribution and issuance from each matter's own documents.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- After a scan that reached every qualifying matter, a follow-up filter on file names, document types, exact phrases or execution flags, or a cap on printed lines, dropped matters, and the candidate set was built only from the filtered or visible output.
- The scan itself missed matters because it was prefiltered by file name or file type, timed out, had a range filter that failed, or was read only partially, and the partial output was treated as the whole store without a rerun or a broader search.
